models._description: (inherit-only) adds 'mail' to the website frontend translation modules so the follow widget's mail terms are translated client-side
(inherit-only) flags website=True in the publisher-warranty _get_message ping so Odoo registers the DB as website-enabled

routes.note: website=True; toggle a partner as follower (message_subscribe / message_unsubscribe) of any mail.thread record from the website follow widget; recaptcha-guarded find-or-create of the partner for public visitors
website=True, readonly=True; given {model:[res_ids]} returns which res_ids the current visitor/user already follows plus {is_user, email}, used by the widget to render Follow vs Unfollow state

security.note: Module declares no ir.model.access, no record rules and no res.groups; the routes operate sudo() on mail.followers / the target record after an explicit record.check_access('read') gate, so visibility is governed by the underlying mail.thread model's ACLs, not by this module.

views.note: No backend act_window views. Ships a single QWeb template website_mail.follow (the input-group follow widget: email field + Follow/Unfollow or Subscribe/Unsubscribe buttons) injected into website pages; 31 XML LOC total.

behavioral_notes.observation: The jsonrpc /website_mail/follow is the follow widget's toggle endpoint. It browses request.env[object].browse(int(id)).exists() (object is the model name + id passed from the widget's data-object/data-id), returns False if the record is gone, then enforces record.check_access('read') -- so a visitor can only follow a record they may read. Partner resolution branches on identity: a logged-in non-public user uses request.env.user.partner_id; a public visitor's typed email is run through record.sudo()._partner_find_from_emails_single([email], no_create=...) where no_create is driven by the recaptcha result (see next note) -- i.e. a successful captcha allows find-OR-create of a res.partner from the email, a failed/absent captcha only finds an existing one. The message_is_follower flag inverts the action: if already follower it calls record.sudo().message_unsubscribe(partner_ids) and returns False; otherwise it stashes partner_ids[0] into request.session['partner_id'] and calls record.sudo().message_subscribe(partner_ids) returning True. So one public route both subscribes and unsubscribes a partner against any mail.thread record's mail.followers, the create-side-effect being a new res.partner for an unknown captcha-verified email.

For a public (website) visitor the controller wraps self.env['ir.http']._verify_request_recaptcha_token('website_mail_follow') in try/except: on any exception no_create=True, on success no_create=False, and that boolean is forwarded to _partner_find_from_emails_single. This means the captcha does not block the follow outright -- it only decides whether an unrecognized email is allowed to mint a brand-new res.partner (anti-spam: bots that fail the captcha can still toggle following of an already-known partner but cannot create partner records). The action token name 'website_mail_follow' is the same string the front-end Follow interaction passes to recaptcha.getToken(...), so server and client agree on the captcha action. This find-or-create-vs-find-only branching is invisible to metadata.

is_follower resolves the acting partner without authentication: a non-public user -> request.env.user.partner_id; a public user -> request.env['res.partner'].sudo().browse(request.session['partner_id']) IF a previous /website_mail/follow stored that session key (this is how an anonymous follower is remembered across the page after subscribing). For each requested model it sudo()._read_group's mail.followers filtered by res_model / res_id in the given ids / partner_id == the resolved partner, and collects the matched res_ids; _read_group naturally drops non-matching rows. It returns a two-element list: [{'is_user': user != public_user, 'email': partner.email or ''}, {model: [followed_res_ids]}]. The route is readonly=True (no write side-effects) and is what lets the widget pre-render Follow vs Unfollow and pre-fill the email box on load.

behavioral_notes.element: publisher_warranty.contract._get_message website flag + ir.http frontend translations
behavioral_notes.observation: Two tiny inherit-only side-effects beyond the routes: publisher_warranty.contract._get_message() super-extends the periodic Odoo publisher-warranty/update ping payload with msg['website']=True, so Odoo's update server learns this database runs a website (telemetry-style flag, not a runtime behavior of the widget). Separately ir.http._get_translation_frontend_modules_name() appends 'mail' to the list of modules whose terms are exported to the website (frontend) translation bundle -- without it the follow widget's mail-owned strings would not be translatable on public pages. Neither is expressible as a field/route in metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (OWL/JS public.interactions follow widget) -- metadata gap #3
behavioral_notes.observation: From frontend/website_mail.frontend.json: present=true, 2 JS files, 0 XML templates, 0 OWL components, registry_adds ['public.interactions.edit:website_mail.follow','public.interactions:website_mail.follow'], no patches/services, bundles {web.assets_frontend:2, web.assets_inside_builder_iframe:1}. The Follow public.interaction (static/src/interactions/follow.js) binds to #wrapwrap[.js_follow], on load RPCs /website_mail/is_follower to set isUser + toggle each .js_follow block, validates the email regex client-side, fetches a google_recaptcha token for action 'website_mail_follow' (and a turnstile_captcha hidden input if present), then RPCs /website_mail/follow with id/object/message_is_follower/email/token and flips the DOM to subscribed. follow.edit.js is the website-builder (edit-mode) variant. The interactive subscribe/unsubscribe UX, email validation and captcha handshake live entirely in static/src, outside Python metadata.

external_integrations.notes: No outbound HTTP/SDK/API keys of its own. google_recaptcha (surfaced through website) verifies the follow token server-side; all other coupling is internal Odoo (mail.followers, res.partner, website session/request).

capabilities: Let Website Visitors Follow a Published Record (self-service subscribe/unsubscribe to its updates)
Capture Visitor Email as a Contact on Follow (recaptcha-gated res.partner creation)
Show Per-Visitor Follow State on Public Pages
Remember Anonymous Followers Across the Session
value_streams: Follow-on-Website: visitor sees follow widget on a published mail.thread record -> enters email (captcha) -> partner found/created -> message_subscribe adds them to mail.followers -> future record posts notify them; toggling again message_unsubscribe removes them
information_concepts: the followed mail.thread record (any published business document)
organization: (none) module defines no res.groups; access governed by the target record's own ACLs via check_access('read')
policies: A visitor may only follow a record they can read (record.check_access('read') before any subscribe)
Public visitors: recaptcha 'website_mail_follow' success required to mint a new res.partner from an unknown email; failure -> find-only (no_create)
Anonymous follower identity persisted in request.session['partner_id'] (no login required)
All follower reads/writes done sudo() after the access gate (mail.followers is otherwise privileged)
stakeholders: Website designer/editor (drops the follow widget on a page via the edit-mode interaction)
Record owner / publisher (gains followers who receive the record's mail.thread notifications)
metrics: is_subscriber / is_user state surfaced to the widget (engagement signal)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_mail is a thin mediating-technology (Stabell & Fjeldstad value network) layer on the website platform: it connects an open population of web visitors to a published business record by letting them self-subscribe as followers and, in doing so, captures each visitor's email as a res.partner contact. Like its parents website and mass_mailing (both network / 3.0 in this corpus) its worth grows with participants -- more visitors following more published records -- rather than via a sequential transformation (chain) or a diagnostic problem-solving cycle (shop). activity_class is primary because the follow widget is a demand-side audience-capture/engagement service the public website delivers, not a back-office support function; it turns anonymous traffic into addressable, opted-in contacts on the firm's mail.thread records. apqc_category 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services (3.4 Develop and manage marketing communications / lead-and-contact capture) fits because the artifact is a marketing/audience-relationship channel -- subscribing visitors to a record's updates and harvesting contact emails -- i.e. demand-side relationship building, mirroring website_links and mass_mailing in this set. The underlying mail notification engine is itself support infrastructure, but website_mail is the public-facing operational tool that recruits the audience, hence primary here.

standard_capabilities: Drop-in website Follow widget (QWeb template website_mail.follow) on any page bound to a mail.thread record
Public subscribe/unsubscribe toggle of a partner against the record's followers (one jsonrpc route)
Per-visitor follow-state lookup for a batch of records (readonly route) to render Follow vs Unfollow
recaptcha-gated find-or-create of a res.partner from the visitor's email (anti-spam contact capture)
Anonymous follower memory via session partner_id (no login required)
mail terms exported to the website translation bundle; DB flagged website-enabled in the warranty ping
typical_fits: Newsletter/'follow this page' style opt-in on blog posts, products, events or any published document
Turning website visitors into followers who receive the record's chatter notifications
Lightweight email capture into res.partner without a full registration form
common_gaps: No double opt-in / confirmation email flow -- a single click (post captcha) subscribes immediately
No dedicated unsubscribe landing page or audit of who followed when (relies on raw mail.followers)
Captcha only gates partner creation, not the follow action itself, so an existing partner can be toggled by a bot that fails the captcha
No segmentation/list semantics here (that is mass_mailing); a follow is per-record, not per-mailing-list
Anonymous follower identity is session-bound and lost if the session/cookie is cleared

Whether google_recaptcha (and/or website_cf_turnstile) is actually configured in the target deployment -- without it the no_create branch always wins and unknown emails never create a partner.
Which website templates in downstream modules embed the website_mail.follow snippet (blog/product/event) is resolvable only with those modules installed.
